notes: SVG-based, so CSS-stylable and readable at scale; JSON graph model (cells) is agent-editable for CRUD. Rappid adds print-to-PDF and ready-made ERD-style UI shapes. Needs a browser/DOM (jsdom works headlessly) to render, so it's not a pure-CLI tool.

Graph-theory-first library (built for relationship-heavy data, e.g. social/biological networks). JSON elements array is agent-CRUD-friendly and it has a headless mode for server-side layout/export. Default styling is more 'network diagram' than 'polished ERD' — needs custom styling work to look boardroom-ready.

Best-in-class layout algorithms (tree/force-directed/layered) and handles large graphs well, but Canvas-based rendering hurts accessibility/testability, and it's paid — a real cost/reversibility consideration before committing.

Same engine as the TypeScript entry, evaluated here for plain-JS/no-build embedding (e.g. a static dashboard page). Cited across sources as the default choice for AI-generated diagrams because output is deterministic text.
